However, for achieving typical Tx-band geostastionary satellite requirements, we show here that such arrays present a great number of elements compared to other types of aperiodic distributions

articleTitle: Very long microstrip array feeds of a membrane reflector for the advanced precipitation radar
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Very long microstrip arrays have been developed at the Ku-band and Ka-band frequencies. Each array, having an electrical length of about 110 free-space wavelengths, is used to feed a deployable thin-membrane cylindrical reflector for a spaceborne precipitation radar application. These arrays, designed for 0/spl deg/ and 30/spl deg/ fixed beam directions, achieved peak sidelobes of -20 dB and average sidelobes below -30 dB with peak cross-pol levels below -20 dB. Several unique challenges were encountered during the technology prototype development of these very long arrays, such as the strong coupling between very long power divider lines, the strong leakage radiation from the lengthy transmission lines, and the lack of computer analysis capability of these electrically large arrays.

articleTitle: 5 GHz band LTCC antenna for WMAN applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, 5 GHz band LTCC antenna for WMAN (wireless metropolitan area network) applications is proposed. This antenna employs modified U slot shape. The simulated return loss characteristics of the proposed antenna show the bandwidth (110 MHz for VSWR < 2), while the measured return loss of the antenna reveals the bandwidth of 180 MHz, which is wider than the predicted one (100 MHz) at the center frequency due to various loss mechanisms. Also, the proposed antenna has good unidirectional radiation pattern and its gain is calculated to be +7.2 dBi

articleTitle: Aperture-coupled thin-membrane microstrip array antenna for beam scanning application
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A microstrip array using an aperture-slot-coupling technique with very thin membranes has been developed at the L-band frequency for a beam scanning application. This technology-demonstration array with 4/spl times/2 elements achieved a relatively wide bandwidth of 100 MHz (8%) and /spl plusmn/45/spl deg/ beam scan. Very narrow coupling slots were used with each having an aspect ratio of 160 (conventional slot aspect ratio is between 10 to 30) for coupling through a very thin membrane (0.05 mm thickness). This thin-membrane aperture-coupling technique allows the array antenna elements to be more easily integrated with transmit/receive amplifier (T/R) and phase shifter modules. The paper addresses only the radiator portion of the array. The array and active components will be presented in a separate paper.

articleTitle: Solving boundary value problems using the generalized (partition of unity) finite element method
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The principal contribution of this paper is two folds: (i) it fully details the implementation scheme for implementing GFEM for the Helmholz equation; (ii) it formulates the Nitsche's method (S. Fernandez-Mendez and A. Huerte, 2004) for implementing the Dirichlet boundary condition. This paper proceeds along the following lines; in the next section, we formulate the problem. Here we introduce the concepts and implementation of GFEM. Then, we prescribe the manner in which various boundary conditions can be implemented. Finally, we demonstrate the accuracy and convergence of the GFEM via a series of analytical comparisons

articleTitle: Comparison of performance of artificial magnetic conductors at L-band
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper we investigate and compare the performance of two types of AMC structures. In particular we consider the effectiveness of each AMC at suppressing TM and TE surfaces at L-band. Design guidelines and trade-offs associated with each structure are given. We also provide experimental results to confirm the effectiveness of each AMC structures and our theoretical evaluations

articleTitle: A calibration technique for measurements of reflection from an open-ended waveguide
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A simple calibration technique is presented for the measurement of the reflection coefficients of an open-ended waveguide. The accuracy of this calibration can be improved by using a waveguide isolator or attenuator between the adapter and the directional coupler. This calibration technique can be further improved by using the time domain gating feature of a vector network analyzer. The admittance of the open-ended waveguide has been measured using this calibration technique at X band and Ku band. The measured results show good agreement with the calculated ones and with those measured using waveguide calibration kits or TRL calibration kits. The calibration technique can be extended to other frequency bands provided that waveguide directional couplers and isolators at those frequency bands are available. The calibration technique can be used for measurements of dielectric permittivity and permeability using an open-ended waveguide system.

articleTitle: Modified wave-front method in 3D electromagnetic field analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Currently there are two main numerical schemes to solve large and sparse finite element matrix equations, one is the direct approach like the Gauss-style method, the other one is the iteration approach. The wave-front method is a kind of special Gauss method. Though the front method is famous for its efficient computation characteristics, it can only be utilized to solve regular finite element matrix equations, i.e, not changeable-degree node problems such as mechanical finite element analysis and is seldom employed in low-frequency EM analysis using FEM because of the change-degree node problem. In this paper, the modified wave-front approach is presented for changeable-degree node problems from 3D eddy current computation, and good agreement between numerical and experimental results are obtained.

articleTitle: Remembering Phillip H. Smith on his 100/sup th/ birthday
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Phillip H. Smith, inventor of the well-known Smith chart, died in Berkeley Heights, New Jersey, on August 29, 1987, at the age of 82. Numerous biographical articles have already been published about Smith, his life, his chart, and his other achievements. The goal of this biographical article is to help us remember Smith on his 100/sup th/ birthday.

articleTitle: Broadband antenna array pattern synthesis with specified null constraints
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper a pattern synthesis technique for broadband antenna array is presented. The technique allows the designer to place a controlled null anywhere in a predetermined antenna pattern with the capability to specify the frequency response in the look direction. It has the potential for parallel processing to increase computational speed in real time

articleTitle: A directivity comparison between hemispherical and planar arrays
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Hemispherical arrays are charming in receiving and processing multiple signals with wide space distributions, especially in integrated navigation systems. In this paper the directivity of a hemispherical array is compared with several kinds of planar array. It shows that the hemispherical array has an attractive scanning directivity performance through the hemi-space above earth plane, especially with small numbers of elements. The effect of element pattern, element number and minimal element spacing is discussed.

articleTitle: A integration version for polarization diversity of microstrip patch antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Four different arrangements of polarization diversity microstrip patch antennas that are suitable for mobile terminal applications have been investigated. Both experimental and calculated results are given, showing that the coupling and the correlative coefficient of signals depend on the relative polarization directions, the distance between two antennas and the /spl epsiv//sub r/ of the substrate used for the microstrip patch antennas. For the sake of coupling, correlative coefficient and space limitations, the back-to-back integration configuration is relatively better to put into a mobile terminal (e.g., laptops and wireless network cards) and the cross-patch antennas are potentially very good for handsets.

articleTitle: Robust direction finding for uniform circular array with mutual coupling
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In scenarios which are common in radar surveillance, cellular telephony etc., the natural choice is a uniform circular array (UCA). However, UCA presents new challenges that manifest themselves in terms of stronger mutual coupling effects. The motivation of this paper is to suggest a knowledge-aided direction finding (DF) method for the UCA in the presence of mutual coupling.

articleTitle: A 2-D Floquet boundary condition for time-domain finite element analysis of periodic geometries
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, we outline a derivation for an absorbing boundary condition (ABC) that, when used with a recently developed FEM-TD formulation, is capable of effectively truncating the computational domain due to higher-order Floquet modes for electromagnetic simulations of infinite periodic structures in 2D. We demonstrated the accuracy of the new ABC, as well as indicating that the inclusion of this rather complicated ABC in the FEM-TD formulation appears to maintain stable time marching, even for a very large time step.

articleTitle: Folded-notch dual band ultra-wideband antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The new folded-notch half-disk antenna supports the dual bands of 2.4-2.5 and 3.1-10.6 GHz without increasing the size of the original UWB half-disk antenna covering only the UWB band. The parametric study demonstrated the effectiveness of controlling the location of the frequency notch and width of the additional operating band. The measured radiated power showed approximately 10 dB suppression at 2.6 GHz. The antenna has good impedance matching over both bands and an omni-directional radiation pattern. The link response showed a linear phase and narrow pulse width. This antenna structure is a good candidate to support both IEEE 802.11g wireless LAN and indoor/outdoor UWB mobile applications.

articleTitle: Radar signature control of wind turbine generators
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Many of the prime locations for wind farms in the UK are on exposed landscapes close to regional airports. However, planning permission for such installations is often being denied because the moving blades of the wind turbines interfere with the operation of airport radar systems. Airport surveillance radars track the position and speed of aircraft in their surrounding airspace using pulsed Doppler radar techniques. The filtering out of signals from spurious stationary and slow moving targets is relatively straight forward as the associated Doppler shift is zero or below a preset threshold. However, when an airport radar receives returns from a wind turbine installation, the motion of the blades can impart to the radar signal a significant Doppler shift that is comparable with that expected from an aircraft. Hence, techniques for reducing the scattering from wind turbines are being actively researched and one approach that we are investigating is the use of active radar absorbing structures based on the concept of a phase-switched screen (PSS) (Tennant, A. and Chambers, B., Proc SPIE, vol.538, 2004; Chambers and Tennant, IEE Proc. Radar Sonar and Navig., vol.149, no.5, p.243-7). We report experimental results obtained from a scaled model windmill with PSS blades operating in conjunction with a 10 GHz Doppler radar system.

articleTitle: Efficient EMI characterization of unshielded buildings
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A statistical analysis method is developed, applicable to simulations and physical experiments, for EM coupling into complex, unshielded buildings. Time-domain electromagnetic field characteristics are presented to quantify the coupling which can then be related to EMI problems in electronic equipment from physical experiments. Several representative buildings with Ethernet network, wireless network, power cabling, lights, HVAC, walls, roof and other common components are analyzed to demonstrate the applicability.

articleTitle: A fast full-wave algorithm to generate low order electromagnetic scattering models
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Segmentation by primary phase factors shows great promise as a tool to accelerate scattering applications. The results show that SPPF-FMOR-PFFT rapidly gencrates accurate full-wave reduced order models that can characterize the scattering from "electromagnetically large" targets over desired frequency ranges with a frequency dependent incident field mid output selection vector. For some of our examples, these results proved to be 10000 times better than previous methods.

articleTitle: Experiment and simulation investigation on performance of discrimination networks for conductive electromagnetic noise
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise is classified into two categories: one is radiated emission and the other is conducted emission. In this paper investigation into the performance of discrimination networks for conductive electromagnetic noise is performed by means of experiment and simulation. Comparisons between experiment and simulation results show good agreement. Further research on other influences on performance is also presented. It is proved that the results in the paper can be utilized in solving conductive EMI.

articleTitle: A new solution expressed in terms of UTD coefficients for multiple diffractions by buildings considering spherical-wave incidence
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new solution expressed in terms of uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) coefficients for the prediction of the multiple diffraction produced by an array of perfectly conducting buildings considering spherical-wave incidence is presented. Buildings are supposed to have rectangular cross sections and the mentioned solution, validated with numerical results from technical literature, is obtained by a recursion relation so that a successive use of UTD, diffraction in the transition zone is avoided, achieving an easier final formulation which significantly reduces the computing time over existing solutions. The result could find application in the planning of microcellular mobile radio systems to predict a more realistic path loss.

articleTitle: A switched sector beam planar antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A planar dipole array antenna which can achieve four sector radiation patterns in the azimuth plane is presented. The antenna is composed of four double-sided printed dipoles arranged symmetrically around the center feed probe. The quarter-wavelength parallel strips line is particularly designed to play different roles in the sector beamforming. A high directivity sector beam can be obtained through the use of appropriate switches placed between the dipole elements and the feed network. Prototypes of the proposed antenna operating in the 2.4GHz band were designed and constructed. Measured and simulated results are used to demonstrate the performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Electrically small transmitting loops
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present data measured by the author and his colleagues (field strength for ground wave and for near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS)), for comparison with simulation. Near fields will be specifically addressed, since near fields are of current interest with regard to human exposure to RF fields and for EMC

articleTitle: A modified standard site method to reduce the effect of a finite-size ground plane
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This study proposes a new calibration method which can reduce antenna factor variations obtained by using the standard site method in a finite-size ground plane. The investigation has been performed numerically with the method of moments in the horizontal and vertical polarizations. Furthermore, the influences of ground size in calibration measurement are analyzed and a new calibration model is also carried out.

articleTitle: A modified PIFA with a small ground plane
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper presents a study on a modified planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) with a small ground plane (7mm /spl times/ 12mm) mounted on a printed circuit board (PCB) of a mobile telephone handset (40mm /spl times/ 100mm) operating at 5.2 GHz. Whilst it inherits the attractive features of PIFA, such as compact size and low profile, the modified antenna exhibits low coupling to the PCB.

articleTitle: Indoor antenna diversity testbed
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper presents a high precision testbed for evaluating antenna diversity techniques in an indoor environment. Details concerning mechanical, electrical and electronics hardware and associated measurement software are described. Initial measurement results for two Bluetooth modules operating with co-polar and cross-polar monopole antennas in the ISM 2.4 GHz band are given.

articleTitle: Small quad-band WLAN antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A novel multi-band printed antenna, ideal for all IEEE 802.11 wireless local area network (WLAN) systems, is presented. It operates well in all frequency bands (2.45, 4.9, 5.25 and 5.775 GHz) allocated worldwide for IEEE 802.1 1a, b, g and j wireless computer systems, demonstrating a return loss >10 dB, an excellent efficiency and a wide radiation pattern. The antenna is printed on a thin (0.8 mm), low cost substrate FR4 using standard microstrip fabrication techniques at a very low cost, and hence it does not require extra processes for mounting or connecting it to the transceiver board. Its very small footprint area (only 10/spl times/10 mm) makes it the smallest quad-band WLAN antenna available yet. The antenna is based on a unique layout of two bent printed strips in which one strip bends around the other and their terminal segments are closer to each other than the rest.

articleTitle: Study of SAR reduction with split ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, we use the split ring resonators (SRR) to reduce the EM interaction between a dipole antenna and a muscle cube. By properly choosing the geometric parameters of SRR, the permeability can be negative at 900MHz and 1.8GHz. It is found that the specific absorption rate (SAR) in the muscle cube can be reduced by placing the designed SRR between the dipole antenna and the muscle cube. The performance of the antenna with SRR is also studied. Numerical results are demonstrated to validate the effect of SAR reduction.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable ultra-thin EBG absorbers using conducting polymers
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new design concept is presented for reconfigurable ultra-thin EBG absorbers that employ FSS screens made from conducting polymer materials. A robust GA technique was developed and successfully applied to evolve optimal designs for the ultra-thin EBG absorbers. Design examples of a single-band and a dual-band reconfigurable EBG absorber are presented.

articleTitle: Dual dipole imaging array for MIR and ECE imaging
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Two dual dipole antennas have been designed in the frequency range of 85-95 GHz and 100-135 GHz for use as imaging array elements for magnetic fusion plasma microwave imaging reflectometry (MIR) and electron cyclotron emission imaging (ECEI) diagnostics, respectively. The antenna pattern is of primary importance for these applications, with emphasis on clean antenna patterns and low sidelobe levels for low interchannel crosstalk, tight channel spacing to minimize interchannel spacing in the plasma, and wide instantaneous bandwidth for real time 2D imaging. The extremely high temperature of the imaged plasma (>10 million degrees), means that a low receiver noise temperature is not critical as long as it is sufficiently low (/spl les/20000 degrees) to facilitate absolute calibration. The simulated and measured antenna patterns are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Hybrid S-parameters for analysis of mixed RF-digital circuits subject to external electromagnetic interference
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: We extend the port analysis technique to accommodate external plane wave coupling. In other words, we propose a frequency domain method which overcomes the CPU bottleneck of time domain techniques and concurrently yields increased accuracy as compared to MTLT. As part of this formalism we introduce additional hybrid S-parameters to establish a link between the existing board ports and external plane waves. Thus, we can handle both on-board and off-board EMI problems simultaneously. This approach can be easily integrated into circuit solvers such as HSPICE and Advanced Design System (ADS, Agilent Technologies). This is achieved by exporting new hybrid S-parameters. The method allows both time domain simulations via broadband network characterization and harmonic balance simulation of nonlinear RF components.

articleTitle: A frequency agile floating-patch MEMS antenna for 42 GHz applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A novel frequency agile floating-patch MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical system) antenna is proposed for 42 GHz applications. The floating-patch MEMS antenna is fabricated on a high resistivity silicon (HRS) substrate using surface micromachining technology. Simulation and experimental results for reflection coefficients and radiation patterns are presented.

articleTitle: Multi-element patch antenna integration into laptops for multi-standard applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper we present an integration procedure of low profile microstrip planar antennas into laptop computers. An antenna system has been designed to be accommodated in the space available behind the LCD matrix of a 14" screen size laptop. A prototype of a multi-element antenna arrangement with a total of 19 elements has been designed, fabricated and tested. It can be used in the GSM1800, UMTS, IEEE 802.11b/Bluetooth and HiperLAN2 standards. The radiation pattern, the input reflection coefficient and the mutual coupling between elements indicate that such a system can be used for multi-standard operation.

articleTitle: The effects of spherical conformity on a wideband L-probe circular patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper has described the theoretical design of a wideband circular L-probe patch antenna covering the ISM band of 2.4GHz. To increase the effective radiation area, the antenna is spherically conformed. To overcome the dielectric material cracking in the commercial microstrip due to the spherical distortions, an air dielectric is assumed, making the design of the antenna very simple and inexpensive. A grid pattern is overlayed on a planar 1.6mm thick commercial grade piece of aluminium cut to a circle with a radius of 100mm. This material is spherically conformed and the distortions measured to become the basis of the spherical conformal ground plane and the benchmark of the conformal element design. The different S/sub 11/ responses of the antenna are shown for different values of the element radius. The radiation pattern for the conformal antenna design shows an increase in the effective radiation area when compared to the flat antenna design. The conformal design also has a response similar to a /spl lambda//4 monopole with a maximum gain of 6dB.

articleTitle: Comparison between planar arrays of perforated DRAs and microstrip patches
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An array of dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) elements is formed by perforating a dielectric substrate with a lattice of holes. The performance of a 64-element prototype array designed at 25 GHz was compared to a corresponding array of microstrip patches. The perforated DRA array demonstrates a gain improvement of 1 dB and a broader gain bandwidth than the microstrip patch array. This technique of fabricating DRA using perforations eliminates the need to position and bond individual DRA elements in an array.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of miniature silicon square spiral chip antenna for implantable bio-MEMS sensors
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, a miniature (1x1 mm) printed square spiral chip antenna for contact-less powering and RF telemetry from implantable bio-MEMS sensors is characterized at 235 MHz. The antenna is fabricated on a high resistivity silicon wafer and has a serrated ground plane on the opposite side to mitigate image current effects. The experimental results include the radiation patterns of the chip antenna and the received signal strength at the output of a larger (10x10 mm) printed square spiral pick-up antenna

articleTitle: A class of physical optics-SVD derived basis functions for solving electromagnetic scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A novel procedure is presented for solving electromagnetic scattering problems in a computationally efficient and numerically rigorous manner. It is based on the use of universal bases which are obtained by applying the SVD procedure to physical optics derived basis functions. These bases, which are constructed completely avoiding any MoM-type approach, can be used for any angle of incidence and lead to a matrix whose dimensions are relatively small. Moreover, it can be shown that the matrix dimensions are weakly dependent upon the size of the scatterer

articleTitle: Center-feed comprised of E to H-plane cross-junctions in an alternating-phase fed single-layer slotted waveguide array
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper demonstrates the reflection suppression over a wideband of the feed waveguide which uses E-to-H-plane cross-junctions in the alternating-phase fed single-layer waveguide array. The FEM analysis is conducted using HFSS for each component as well as the full structure of the array, which has more than 30dBi gain.

articleTitle: Microstripline fed circular sector dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A microstripline fed circular sector dielectric resonator antenna is investigated. A 180/spl deg/ sector of a cylindrical DR on a ground plane has been used for the study. The proposed configuration offers an increase in bandwidth (24%) with broadside radiation pattern. In addition, the configuration offers simple feed structure, compact size and thus easy integration with handheld communication equipment.

articleTitle: Analysis of the surface current distributions in a dual band planar antenna for passive RFID tag
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Measurements are presented on the performance of a novel dual band passive RFID tag antenna constructed from a planar structure which operates at the frequencies of 868 MHz and 2.4 GHz. A study of the surface current distributions of the antenna has been carried out to achieve the optimal location and coupling of the transponder chip. Results are presented for the surface current distributions, resonant frequencies and read range. Data for the study are calculated using CST microwave studio which applies the finite integral technique on approximated perfect boundaries of the planar structure.

articleTitle: Variational principle in the problem of radiation from a waveguide with impedance flange
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The characteristics of radiation from a semi-infinite waveguide with an impedance flange are analyzed using the variational approach. Stationary functionals are developed for the input admittance, radiation field, and field of surface waves along the flange. The single-mode approximation was used for derivation of simple applied formulas.

articleTitle: A wide-band dual-polarized VHF microstrip antenna for global /sup s/ensing of sea ice thickness
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A VHF microstrip patch antenna was developed to achieve a bandwidth of 45 MHz (300%) from 127 MHz to 172 MHz with dual-linear-polarization capability. This microstrip antenna uses foam substrates and dual stacked patches with capacitive probe feeds to achieve wide bandwidth. Four such capacitive feeds were used to achieve dual polarization with less than -20 dB of cross-polarization level. Twenty-four shorting pins were used on the lower patch to achieve acceptable isolation between the four feed probes. This antenna has a measured gain of 8.5 dB at 137 MHz and 10 dB at 162 MHz. By using the method of moments technique, multipath scattering patterns were calculated when the antenna is mounted on the outside of a Twin Otter aircraft.

articleTitle: High-voltage and high current measurement techniques for a very low frequency (VLF) composite bushing
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: High voltage and high current testing methods for a very low frequency (VLF) composite bushing is presented. These measurements are performed at the Edgar Beauchamp High Voltage Test Facility (EBHVTF) in Dixon, California.

articleTitle: A novel Vivaldi fed reflector impulse radiating antenna (IRA)
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Impulse radiating antennas (IRA) have been used to radiate electromagnetic energy in a very short period of time. A method of moments (MoM) based software, the Hybrid EFIE and MFIE Iterative (HEMI), developed at UCLA, is employed to calculate the far-field patterns and the current distributions. We used a 57cm parabolic reflector with a focal length to diameter ratio (F/D) of 0.40 in our HEMI model.

articleTitle: Modified simply sparse method for electromagnetic scattering by PEC
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, the multilevel simply sparse method (MLSSM) is presented to improve the performance of fast direct solvers for integral equations. The SSM is a general, physically motivated compression algorithm for integral equation formulations of electromagnetic phenomena. An important feature of the algorithm is the ease with which it can be applied to diverse scattering and radiation configurations. In this paper, the MSSM is used to compress various integral equations including the electric field integral equation (EFIE), magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) and combined field integral equation (CFIE). All of these IE were compressed into a sparse format and compared to the compressed format of the MLFMM. Also, the work presented consists of the multilevel implementation of the SSM (MLSSM) that will further reduce the memory usage.

articleTitle: Half disc element dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper we study the properties of a half disc dipole ultra wideband (UWB) antenna. The antenna is numerically analyzed using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) technique. The results obtained for the half disc UWB dipole antenna are similar to that obtained for the circular dipole antenna; the only difference in the case of the half disc dipole antenna is the reduction in size of the antenna.

articleTitle: Self-structuring antenna concept for FM-band automotive backlight antenna design
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The study of the SSA has shown much promise for use in an automobile environment; however, the addition of the necessary switch technology adds a new level of complexity to existing antenna systems. Some of the benefits of the SSA can be obtained with existing systems by using the SSA concept to design a fixed antenna. This work uses the principles of self-structuring antennas to design a fixed automotive backlight antenna. A genetic algorithm (GA) is utilized in this design, with a cost function optimizing both VSWR and gain

articleTitle: A novel time reversal method for target detection in cluttered media
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A cluttered environment with highly scattering objects significantly enhances the difficulty for detecting targets using electromagnetic waves. Time reversal methods have been developed in acoustic wave propagation. It has been shown that the super resolution focusing effect in acoustic wave propagation can also be achieved electromagnetic wave propagation. We present a novel time reversal method that nullifies the scattering objects to allow automatic focusing of the propagated electromagnetic wave on a target that is to be detected. Numerical simulations using the FDTD method have been carried out. The results show that the method significantly enhances the dynamic range of target detection in a highly scattering environment and could substantially increase target detectability.

articleTitle: Optimization of aperiodic array patterns using GA and SDA
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper the author makes use of the advantage of broad search space of genetic algorithms (GA) for finding an ultimate solution, together with the preciseness of the optimum given by the steepest descent algorithm (SDA). The problem analyzed in this paper is an extension of the previous work on optimization of aperiodic array patterns. The optimization procedure proposed in this paper is, first, to find an initial position by using GA, and then by using that initial position, try to find an ultimate solution by SDA. The author has succeeded in reducing the sidelobe levels by 4 dB compared with those obtained by using only SDA.

articleTitle: Bandwidth improvement for crossed-dipole type antennas using a tuning plate
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Significant bandwidth improvement is achieved on the crossed-dipole antenna using the tuning plates. The tuning plate was tested on the foursquare and fourpoint antennas. The test models demonstrate that a tuning plate increases the bandwidth of crossed-dipole type antennas up to 25% over that for the same antenna without the tuning plate. The foursquare and fourpoint antennas with the tuning plate are good candidates for dual-polarized, multi-functional antenna applications and for MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Small, planar, ultra-wideband antennas with top-loading
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new top-loaded ultra-wideband antenna covering the 2.4-10.6 GHz impedance bandwidth (VSWR<2.5) and the 2.05-11.6 GHz UWB bandwidth with nearly constant radiated power was introduced. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for backward compatibility of IEEE 802.11g in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, as well as providing an indoor/outdoor ultra-wideband frequency range of 3.1-10.6 GHz. In addition, it can be used for both multi-band OFDM and impulse UWB applications.

articleTitle: Proximity-coupled microstrip patch antenna miniaturization using new fractal geometry
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: For more antenna miniaturization, we present a novel fractal geometry that allows a decrease in the resonance frequency without occupying more space, while retaining a radiation pattern similar to that of a normal square patch. Also, to improve the inherently narrow bandwidth of the patch fractal antenna, a proximity-coupled feed is implemented. The performance is demonstrated by simulation based on a numerical analysis with the finite element method (FEM) and a practical application to personal communication services (PCS).

articleTitle: A multi-functional stacked patch antenna for wireless power beaming and data telemetry
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A multi-functional stacked patch antenna is introduced for a possible wireless power beaming and data telemetry application. The proposed antenna operates at 5.8 GHz with 10 dBi gain, and 18% bandwidth. At a lower frequency, around 2.45 GHz, the antenna operates as a planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) with 4 dBi gain and 3.2% bandwidth. Switching between the two regimes of operation can be achieved using PIN diodes. It is proposed that the antenna can be used for wireless power reception in sensors at 5.8 GHz and for data telemetry between sensors or between sensor and control station at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Ladder antennas for dual circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A novel radiator, a ladder antenna, is proposed for a dual circularly polarized (CP) antenna. The ladder is formed by microstrip lines printed on a grounded dielectric substrate. The antenna is excited at the ladder-side ends: F/sub R/ and F/sub L/. By changing the excitation points of FR and we can select the rotational sense of the CP radiation. In this paper, three types of ladder antennas are numerically analyzed: they are ladders along the y-axis, along the x-axis and a ladder array. The y-axis ladder is a prototype. After investigating the x-axis ladder, we realize the ladder array.

articleTitle: Crown-Sierpinski microstrip antenna: further reduction of the size of a Crown Square Fractal
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, the first resonant frequencies of Crown square and Crown-Sierpinski antennas are compared with the well known nearly square and Sierpinski carpet antennas. It has been shown that the two presented antennas have lower first resonant frequencies that causes a noticeable reduction in the size of the antennas. In exchange of size minimizing, the axial ratio of the Crown square and Crown-Sierpinski micro strip antennas is degraded

articleTitle: An integrated coaxial circular-polarised OMJ/OMT for dual-band feed applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A novel integrated coaxial circularly-polarised OMJ/OMT (orthogonal-mode junction/orthogonal-mode transducer) structure is proposed for dual-band feed applications. The new structure is simple and compact with all the phasers, hybrids and power dividers built on the surface of the inner conductor. A section of coaxial waveguide engraved with these components performs all the functions of a large number of separate devices, such as polariser, OMJ, rectangular waveguide arms, power divider and OMT. Further, this structure is suitable for die-casting and could be used for mass production. The bridge ridge directional coupler used in the integrated CP OMJ/OMT is a new structure. It offers a new method for design of a directional coupler using a ridge waveguide at its common narrow wall.

articleTitle: Radiation pattern measurements of small isolated antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: We present a system developed for measuring small antennas; in particular, for measuring their radiation patterns in a spherical format. The antenna under test (AUT) is positioned with an elevation over the azimuth positioner made entirely from dielectric materials. The test signal can be fed from a built-in generator powered by a battery. Owing to the elimination of the feeding cable normally used in an antenna measuring setup, measurements are run in conditions that reconstruct the actual operational environment with accurate results. The measuring time is short, as the rotational speed of the dielectric positioner is sufficiently fast. With the use of a microwave backward projection technique, it is possible to estimate the field distribution inside a lossy object placed next to the AUT, thus providing a quick, nondosimetric evaluation of the SAR distribution inside a phantom head.

articleTitle: A space-time processing approach to joint estimation of signal frequency and 2-D direction of arrival
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper, a new method is proposed for joint estimation of the signal frequencies and 2D direction of arrival. The method uses temporal data and spatial data to form a time-space DOA matrix, and the three parameters could be obtained from the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of the time-space DOA matrix respectively. Without spectral search, the method is computationally efficient and the estimates of the three parameters are automatically paired. In addition, the method is able to estimate more sources than the number of sensors, and the subarray geometry is flexible so accurate estimations can be obtained by using an appropriate subarray geometry. Simulation results show that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: Antenna measurement facility comparison campaign within the European Antenna Centre of Excellence
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the antenna measurement techniques and facility sharing activity of the Antenna Centre of Excellence (ACE) within the EU's 6'th framework program for research - in particular, the facility comparison campaign with the DTU-ESA 12 GHz validation standard antenna (VAST12).

articleTitle: Evaluation of the quality factor of an electrically small antenna in spheroidal coordinates
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A number of researchers have obtained expressions for the quality factor or "Q" of an antenna. Most of these authors treated the antenna as surrounded by a spherical surface. A spherical surface conforms to the geometry of very few antennas. Here we derive the corresponding expressions for the Q of an electrically small antenna surrounded by an spheroidal surface that is either prolate or oblate. In this way we can better treat the effects of aspect ratio. Prolate spheroids should better represent most antennas, which are long and thin. Oblate spheroids should represent antennas in the shape of a disk. We also present analytic expressions for the value of Q for spheroids in the limit of very small electrical length. The expressions become equal to that of the sphere in the appropriate limit. We explore some of the results from analytic expressions for prolate and oblate spheroids when compared to a sphere

articleTitle: 5.8 GHz dual-polarized aperture-coupled microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The paper presents the design of a dual-polarized aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna suitable for passive 5.8 GHz radio frequency identification (RFID) applications. The antenna provides two orthogonal ports with nearly 30 dB isolation and crosspolarization levels of nearly 20 dB for both ports. Using the orthogonal ports, both transmit and receive functions can be implemented on the same antenna. This type of antenna could be very useful for RFID transponders which have to receive energy from an RFID reader and send back identification information.

articleTitle: A new three-dimensional vector parabolic equation approach for modeling radio wave propagation in tunnels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new three-dimensional (3D) vector parabolic equation method (PEM) is proposed to study the propagation of electromagnetic waves in tunnels, which is particularly useful for modeling wave propagation in tunnels with traffic obstructions. It allows full wave treatment of the 3D problem which is not possible by its scalar version. Vector fields are presented in terms of three unknown scalar functions which are coupled through boundary conditions on the tunnel walls and divergence-free condition of electromagnetic fields. Numerical results for empty and obstructed tunnels are presented.

articleTitle: A low-profile broadband strip-line balun
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The paper describes the design of a broadband balun with a multilayer coupled strip-line structure for a frequency range from 1.35 GHz to 2.7 GHz. This balun presents progress by providing PCB compatibility, integrated shielding (strip-line), and a relatively compact footprint in comparison with other balun topologies (e.g. microstrip and Lange couplers). The balun is first simulated schematically and electromagnetically using Advanced Design System. The results show good agreement between both sets of simulation data and the measurements results.

articleTitle: Prediction of indoor and outdoor signal strengths from indoor transmitter
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper describes a method for an integrated site-specific radiowave propagation simulation model for both indoor and outdoor building environments. The results of the model are compared to measurements taken from the campus of the University of Arizona at four frequencies: 49, 379, 943 and 1842 MHz. The model accounts for propagation between different floors within the same building as well as propagation from an indoor base station to outdoor receivers.

articleTitle: Novel antenna for mobile terminals based on the chassis-antenna coupling
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In the miniaturization process of mobile terminals, the antenna plays an important role, since the reduction of its size leads to a degradation of some of the radiation properties (e.g., bandwidth and gain). To avoid this problem, the possibility of considering the whole metallic structure of the terminal as part of the antenna has been proposed (Vainikainen, P. et al., IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag., vol.50, no.10, p.1433-44, 2002). As a result, improved radiation behavior can be obtained. We computed the resonant modes of a chassis structure (Antonino-Daviu, E. et al., AP-SA/URSI Symp., 2004) by means of the theory of characteristic modes, defined by R.F. Harrington and J.R. Mautz (1971), and the effect of the coupling of a small antenna on the characteristic modes (resonant modes) behavior was analyzed as well. As shown by Vainikainen et al., the performance of the antenna-chassis combination has a very clear dependency on the chassis resonance. From our knowledge of the properties of the diverse characteristic modes of the chassis, further work has been carried out to design a chassis-antenna structure with improved radiating properties. The paper illustrates the consistent design procedure followed to obtain the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Coaxial-line feed for post-wall waveguide in millimeter wave band
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The authors have proposed a millimeter-wave band interface to a post-wall waveguide through a coaxial structure in order to realize cost-effective 60GHz modules. We have investigated the fabrication tolerance and the reflection characteristics, where PTFE and LTCC substrates are used. Feeding structures are assessed experimentally to fulfill many demands on substrates and manufacturing in millimeter-wave bands.

articleTitle: Interference of digital noise with integrated dipole antenna for inter-chip signal transmission in ULSI
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Interference of digital noise with integrated linear dipole antennas was investigated for inter-chip ultrawideband communication in Si ULSIs (ultra-large scale integrated circuits). Gaussian monocycle pulse signals were transmitted from a linear dipole antenna fabricated on a Si substrate to a receiving antenna fabricated on a separate substrate. Rectangular pulses, as digital noise for interference, were radiated from a transmission line fabricated on another Si chip which was inserted between the transmitting and receiving antennas. The received Gaussian monocycle pulses were distorted by the digital noise radiated from the other chip. It is found that the differential mode Gaussian monocycle pulse was effective in preventing interference.

articleTitle: Mobile communications experiments on dual-band triangular-patch array antenna using a pseudo satellite
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A simple satellite-tracking array antenna for mobile satellite communications aimed at ETS-VIII applications has been discussed. The proposed antenna is constituted of triangular patches sequentially rotated by 120/spl deg/. By successively turning off any one of the patches, it is shown that three beams are created in the conical-cut plane for transmission and reception. Furthermore, the gain can reach more than 5 dBic on the whole azimuth range for an elevation El = 48/spl deg/ in Tokyo. Mobile satellite experiments using the developed antenna and a pseudo satellite are performed. According to the results, the received power is in agreement with the calculations.

articleTitle: On 2D forward-backward spatial smoothing for azimuth and elevation estimation of coherent signals
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The paper presents two-dimensional forward-backward spatial smoothing for estimating the azimuth and elevation of fully coherent sources using a uniform rectangular array (URA). To guarantee the resolvability of K coherent signals for all possible cases, the minimum size of the total URA is 3K/2/spl times/3K/2 for the proposed method and 2K/spl times/2K for the existing forward-only 2D spatial smoothing scheme. Simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel antenna suitable for wireless LAN hub
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An antenna suitable for a WLAN hub is presented. The goal is to create a compact polarization-diversity antenna with conical coverage in both horizontal and vertical polarizations. It is well known that a constant current loop creates such a pattern with the electric field in horizontal polarization and that a monopole creates such dependence with the electric field in vertical polarization. The design presented is original in the way it uses slots for approaching the constant current loop pattern. The vertical polarization is realized by the traditional quarter-wavelength monopole with optional top loading for profile reduction. The antenna has been designed using the finite integration algorithm under CST MWS /spl reg/. It has been realized successfully in the laboratory and measured. Measurement results are compared to simulation results and good agreement is found. The antenna is attractive commercially and has been recently filed as a patent application.

articleTitle: Effect of the finite grounded substrate on the input impedance of the microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The effects of the finite nature of the grounded dielectric slab on the input impedance of the microstrip patch antenna are investigated. The approximate closed-form spatial domain Green's functions of the vector and scalar potentials derived recently for a horizontal electric dipole placed over a finite grounded dielectric slab are used in the method of moments formulation of the microstrip patch antenna. For different substrate sizes, the input impedance and the resonant frequency values are calculated and compared with the experimental and numerical results reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Slotted arrays for low profile mobile DBS antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: We have developed a low profile antenna for the United States (US) DBS mobile market. The antenna utilizes slotted array elements that radiate either right-hand or left-hand circular polarization tilted by 45/spl deg/ off-broadside. The structure, with limited required scan, can render relatively low profile mobile antennas.

articleTitle: A mechanically steerable array antenna with controllable microwave phase shifters at 20 GHz
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A mechanically steerable antenna was designed and developed using an adjustable microwave phase shifter. The dielectric material /spl epsiv//sub /spl tau// = 10 (alumina) was used as the dielectric slab and was placed close to a coplanar TL. Numerical simulations using Ansoft HFSS and Designer were conducted at 20 GHz. For the testing purpose, a 4-element steerable array antenna at 5.8 GHz was fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Miniaturized open-ended radiator based on waveguide filled with uniaxial negative permeability metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The recently introduced concept of waveguide miniaturization using a uniaxial negative permeability metamaterial is extended to the design of a miniaturized open-ended radiator. The reflection coefficient and radiation pattern of such an antenna are investigated numerically and experimentally. The experimental prototype comprises an open-ended evanescent waveguide with a cross-section of 0.2/spl lambda//spl times/0.2/spl lambda/. The waveguide is filled with negative permeability uniaxial metamaterial based on double-ring resonators in the 7 GHz band and excited with a specially designed probe. The measurements reveal an H-plane radiation pattern with 3 dB beamwidth of approximately 100/spl deg/ and return loss of 13 dB across an operating bandwidth of 5%.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis of a plasma column antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Our recent experiments have confirmed that a plasma antenna could operate with characteristics similar to copper antennas when the plasma frequency is sufficiently higher than the operating frequency. The observed gain of the plasma antenna was approximately 3-4 dB lower than that of the copper antenna.

articleTitle: An internal dual band antenna for Bluetooth/DMB applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An internal dual band antenna is proposed for Bluetooth and digital multimedia broadcasting (DMB) services. This novel antenna, fed by a 50 /spl Omega/ coaxial cable, operates at the Bluetooth (2400-2483 MHz) and DMB (2535-2655 MHz) bands, respectively. The size of this antenna is 17/spl times/10 mm/sup 2/ and its height is 7 mm. When this antenna is applied for handset case, the bandwidth of presented antenna is 290 MHz starting from 2400 MHz to 2690 MHz for VSWR <2.0. The simulated and measured results were obtained by considering the antenna with and without the handset case, including battery.

articleTitle: DOA determination by using an antenna system without phase center and MUSIC algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Defining the direction of arrival (DOA) is an important problem in radar surveillance, mobile communications, etc. There are many algorithms to address this. Among them, some of the best known are MUSIC, ESPRIT, MLE. The signal model in those algorithms is based on assuming that the array element signals are similar in both amplitude and phase pattern. The paper presents a new approach to find the DOA by using an antenna system without a phase center and MUSIC algorithm. The antenna system consists of two antenna elements. The phase pattern of the array elements is taken into account. The power spectrum improvement is verified by simulation and the number of detected sources is not limited by the number of antenna elements.

Author Keywords: array of elements without phase center

articleTitle: Far field pattern for rectangular PIFA antenna from the cavity model
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A conventional patch antenna (PA) with its rectangular radiating sheet shorted to a ground plane along the zero potential line forms a rectangular planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA). The PIFA therefore can be considered as an effective compact antenna system with a patch area of less than one-half of usual square patch antenna. It is modelled as a resonant cavity with magnetic walls between the radiating plate and the ground plane. The far field expressions are derived using potential theory with the assumption of magnetic currents flowing around the cavity boundaries. An improved model for the far fields is described which accounts for the PIFA side slots. These affect both the impedance and the pattern. The model agrees well with experiments and gives insight into the behaviour of the impedance and pattern of the general PIFA.

articleTitle: Application of a novel parallel particle swarm optimization to the design of electromagnetic absorbers
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: We presented the synchronous PSO, which is inherently parallel. The parallelism of the synchronous PSO makes practical the design of complex absorbers on clusters of computers. Nonetheless, it is found that parallel PSO must incorporate a special operator not found in standard PSO to keep the population from converging suboptimally to the boundary. This synchronous PSO was applied to optimize multilayer coatings and polygonal absorbers for wide band frequency and/or wide incident range.

articleTitle: Study of the shaped probe on the cup dielectric resonator antenna for bandwidth enhancement
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) are attractive at high frequencies. They can be designed with different shapes, but have the drawback of narrow bandwidths, typically around 10%. A wide range of materials is available to control the size and the bandwidth. One method of excitation is the coaxial probe, which is usually placed inside the DRA. It can be difficult to drill a small hole for the probe in ceramic materials, especially if the hole is close to the wall. Deformation of the DRA geometry from regular shapes can be used to enhance the bandwidth. Instead of drilling a small hole in the DRA, we modify the shape of the DRA to contain an easily machined groove which is large enough to house the shaped probe. Several probe shapes are investigated. It is found that L-, J- or hook-shaped probes can enhance the bandwidth of the DRA and excite a broadside-radiating mode. A single probe achieves a bandwidth around 30%. Using two orthogonal probes excites two orthogonal modes for dual polarization and further enhances the bandwidth. A wideband dually polarized DRA was studied and a bandwidth of 30-50% was achieved.

articleTitle: Amplifying left-handed transmission line media
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Using a one-dimensional structure as the basis for our studies, we have demonstrated that the left-handed nonlinear transmission line (LH NLTL) that we developed for slightly different applications can also, under the correct design conditions, be used for parametric amplification, by which energy in a pump wave at one frequency is transferred to energy in a weak signal wave at another frequency. Our approach could be scaled from its current X-band (10 GHz) form into THz, infrared, or ultimately visible form.

articleTitle: Determination of the multipath delay profile of arrival (/spl tau/OA) through the use of the time correlation and of an array antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Smart antennas have been used more and more to establish the SDMA access technique, reducing the spatial interference in a wireless propagation area. The dual of this problem, in the time domain, refers to the intersymbol interference resulting from the multipath components. The article proposes a way to reduce the intersymbol interference through techniques that use the structure of an antenna array.

articleTitle: Grating lobe suppression by a parasitic dipole layer over a waveguide transverse slot array with reflection-canceling posts
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A unit element consisting of a transverse slot, a post and a pair of parasitic dipoles is proposed for an application in the bore-sight beam antenna array to suppress grating lobes with minimum unit reflection at the waveguide input. The unit is designed with suitable dipole position and dimensions to suppress radiation in the directions of grating lobes in a transverse slot array and with suitable diameter and position of the post to minimize input reflection. The reflection and radiation characteristics of the unit are analyzed by the method of moments (MoM). It is found that larger reflection of a transverse slot can be reduced below -20 dB while its uniform pattern can be suppressed by more than 20 dB in the direction of the grating lobes.

articleTitle: Model-based investigation on MIMO channel capacity in main street of urban microcells
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: We have studied the influence of environmental parameters and of antenna array height and inter-element spacing on MIMO channel capacity. Vertical polarization (VP) and horizontal polarization (HP) have been considered. In general, VP results in more MIMO channel capacity. The results could be useful in designing systems to provide high data. rate services.

articleTitle: Integrated wideband rectangular dielectric resonator antenna for WLAN
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An integrated wideband rectangular dielectric resonator antenna for 5 GHz WLAN is reported. The antenna with small ground plane is probe fed by a pair of magnetic dipole and magnetic loop. The proposed antenna structure exhibits wide input impedance bandwidth of 23.2%, high radiation gain (5 dBi at 5.5 GHz) and unidirectional radiation pattern which is suitable for application in a 5 GHz WLAN system.

articleTitle: Grating of perforated strips as a multi-rejection FSS
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Simple grating of perforated strips is considered. Such a grating with one slot over the period, provides rejection frequency response. The grating with two different slots over the period provides frequency response with two rejection resonances. Simple and strict dependences of quality-factor and location of the resonance on the grating geometry are demonstrated. A numerical example for layered FSS forming quasi-elliptical frequency response is proposed as well.

articleTitle: Convergence acceleration for calculating radiated fields by a vertical electric dipole in the presence of a large sphere
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The solution of the radiation of a vertical dipole in the presence of a large sphere is represented by infinite summation. It is known that the series usually has a convergence problem when both the source and the observation point are on or close to the surface. Also, the series converges slowly when the wavelength in air is much smaller than the radius of the sphere. The continuity of the field expressions on the spherical surface at r=r' in the space is discussed and we give a convergence acceleration method for the infinite summation due to a vertical electric dipole radiating in the presence of a perfectly conducting sphere.

articleTitle: An optimized shaped beam synthesis technique and its implementation
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The Orchard-Elliott shaped beam synthesis technique is modified to improve its performance. The new algorithm can synthesise shaped beams with a large number of array elements and very low ripple level, as small as 0.003 dB, in the shaped region and a controlled sidelobe in the sidelobe region, without convergence problems. A new technique for the implementation of shaped beam antennas is also proposed. In this technique, both phase and amplitude weighting is accomplished in one block using sampling of signals over antenna elements by sampling pulses with adjusted time delays and duty cycles.

articleTitle: On some limitations in the effective number of degrees of freedom achievable in MIMO channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper it is shown a relationship between the effective number of degrees of freedom (ENDF) of a MIMO channel and the number of degrees of freedom (NDF) of the field. In particular, the NDF is an upper bound for the ENDF.

articleTitle: 3-D FDTD modeling of ULF/ELF propagation within the global Earth-ionosphere cavity using an optimized geodesic grid
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: We discuss an emerging application of finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) computational electrodynamics: modeling transient ultra-low frequency (ULF) and extremely low frequency (ELF) propagation within the global Earth-ionosphere cavity. This permits for the first time a direct, three-dimensional, time-domain calculation of round-the-world ULV/ELF propagation accounting for arbitrary horizontal as well as vertical geometrical and electrical inhomogeneities and anisotropies of the excitation, ionosphere, lithosphere, and oceans.

articleTitle: Satellite radio diversity antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Most of the luxury vehicles utilize composite body with no metallic roof, which, in turn, necessitates the use of non-traditional antenna systems and mounting locations. On the other hand, a single SDAR antenna at a sub-optimal location is very unlikely to satisfy system requirements. Multiple antennas in a diversity setting offer a favorable solution for such cases. Two independent antennas combined at the receiver is the focus of this study. The antennas are implemented on two different composite body vehicles, and passive antenna range measurements as well as ride-data reveal that the diversity antenna system has a superb reception quality

articleTitle: A miniature four-arm antenna for tri-band GPS applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper presents a novel miniature GPS antenna which is 3 times smaller than its reference. A particular feature of the antenna is the capability to cover all three GPS bands (L5, L2, L1) instead of the usual L2 and L1 bands.

articleTitle: A helmet mounted GPS antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: GPS receivers have evolved into a necessary component of the modern military because they allow precise positioning of both equipment and troops. In this paper, we present an analysis of a helmet mounted GPS antenna. This includes a performance analysis of a standalone antenna as well as the antenna mounted on a helmet.

articleTitle: Antenna optimization using a hybrid evolutionary programming method
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The fundamentals of a hybridization approach for a class of EA called evolutionary programming (EP) that has recently been applied to circuit optimization problems is explained. Easier implementation and self-adaptation mechanism are some of the advantages of EP compared to other type EA such as the genetic algorithm (GA). However, the hybridization method explained in this paper is equivalently applicable to all other paradigms of EA.

articleTitle: Numerical mode matching method with perfectly matching layer
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The numerical mode matching method (NMM) with the perfectly matching layer (PML) has been presented in this paper to solve electromagnetic fields in stratified media with some possible lossless layers. When the 2D inhomogeneous media is lossy media, the field in this inhomogeneous media can be solved efficiently by using the NMM with the concepts of the general reflection matrix and general transmission matrix. Unfortunately, this method failed in the case of lossless media. In order to make the NMM available in the media with lossless layers, the PML has been introduced into the NMM in this paper to build the truncated absorbing boundary in lossless layers. Some numerical examples have also been given in this paper.

articleTitle: A broadband circularly polarized lightweight antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The presented antenna is lightweight, has a low profile and provides outstanding parameter values over a wide bandwidth. In particular, such good circular polarization across a broad angular range in the forward hemisphere is of great practical value and has been rarely reported on in the literature for such thin antennas to the best of our knowledge. It should be mentioned that the proposed antenna generates very good circular polarization with a use of a single patch thus, clustering elements to achieve very good circular polarization is unnecessary.

articleTitle: RCS predictions and measurements of a full size jet engine model
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Most of the industrial software codes used for the prediction of the radar cross-sections (RCS) of aircraft are based on ray tracing. While ray based methods give useful scattered fields from the skin of the aircraft illuminated by an incident plane wave, they largely fail to predict the returns from onboard cavities, such as the jet engines. As a possible enhancement to these ray-tracing programs, an auxiliary program based on the modal method was developed to predict the scattering of electrically large and complex jet inlets and engines. Monostatic RCS measurements of a 0.706 m diameter test cylinder containing 30 skewed blades mounted on a center shaft with a conical hub have been performed at X-band. The dimensions of the structure and the number and orientation of the blades are consistent with existing jet engines. Good agreement between predictions and measurements verify the developed software and analytical method used.

articleTitle: Bandlimited spectral local-global solution modes for surface integral equations
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper we outline a numerical procedure to determine incident plane wave modes which excite surface current solutions on PEC targets that simultaneously satisfy both local and global boundary conditions. For a requested tolerance /spl epsiv/, the resulting local-global solution (LOGOS) modes are typically localized (to order-/spl epsiv/) within a small section of a large target. It is subsequently shown that this spatial localization facilitates the use of bandlimited functions to represent the spectral LOGOS excitations.

articleTitle: A direct broadcast satellite reception system for automotive OEMs
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Mobile direct broadcast satellite (DBS) reception systems have been on the market for several years. But only recently have companies made a serious effort to offer the public a system that can be installed on their automobiles. These products are currently being offered as aftermarket pods bolted to the top of the vehicle. Public acceptance has been slow, though most vehicle manufacturers agree that quality TV reception in the vehicle, at the right price, is on their list of technologies to have. For the OEM, it is imperative that the satellite TV system be integrated seamlessly into the vehicle roof structure in a manner that preserves the designer's styling. Of equal importance, the system's integration with the vehicle human machine interface (HMI) and the audio/video systems must also be seamless. System manufacturers realize that for their product to sell at any significant volume, it must be integrated into a broad range of popular vehicles.

articleTitle: Optimization of a gangbuster reflectarray antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: In this paper we discuss the optimization of the design, carried out through a pseudo-random optimization algorithm, of a gangbuster reflectarray antenna. The variation of reflection coefficient phase on the reflectarray surface is achieved by varying the length of the local wires in the gangbuster surface. For the optimization, a genetic algorithm has been used to maximize the re-radiated field in a certain direction (e.g., the broadside direction) and to reduce the sidelobe level.

articleTitle: Particle swarm optimization of miniaturized quadrature reflection phase structure for low-profile antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new terminology, quadrature reflection phase structure (QRPS), is defined. Without applying traditional methods, such as effective circuit modeling, a parallel PSO/FDTD (particle swarm optimization/finite difference time-domain) algorithm is utilized to determine a QRPS topology based on its reflection phase characteristics. The optimized QRPS has miniaturized dimensions and provides good performance in a surface wave antenna application. The parallel PSO/FDTD algorithm has the potential to be promising in more complicated QRPS/EBG designs, by exploiting the robustness of the PSO kernel, the accuracy of a full-wave simulator and faster computation due to its parallel implementation.

articleTitle: Compact and broadband rectangular microstrip antenna using stepped U or V-slot
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Various compact and broadband rectangular microstrip antennas using variations of stepped U or V-slots are proposed. These configurations have larger bandwidth, without increasing the total antenna size or thickness.

articleTitle: Dual-band multiple beam antenna system for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band antenna system that is suitable for satellite communications at K/Ka-band frequencies. It employs a minimum number of reflectors, each being fed with multiple feed horns. It is shown that the MBA performance in terms of coverage gain and co-polar isolation can be significantly improved by using optimal designs for the feed horn and the reflector. The performance results of this MBA are compared with conventional designs and the trade-offs are discussed.

articleTitle: Reduction of feed blockage in reflectarray by orthogonally polarized transformation
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A microstrip reflectarray is usually composed of a feed and an array of printed metal patch elements that are slightly different from each other to reflect the incident field into a phase-coherent beam in a prescribed direction. The feed placed in front of the reflectarray causes blockage to the reflected wave. A reflectarray with orthogonally polarized transformation is proposed in an innovative concept developed for blockage reduction. The reflectarray is simulated with valuable data, designed on high performances, and fabricated. About 4 dB gain drop due to feed-blockage may be avoided by this technology, and about a 10 % frequency band may be covered.

articleTitle: Dual-frequency dual-polarized sixteen-element stacked patch microstrip array antenna for soil moisture and sea surface salinity missions
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A dual-polarized dual-band active/passive (radar/radiometer) microstrip array for remote-sensing applications is described.
